note: Scored members are evacetrapib, DRL-17822 and rocacetrapib (CKD-519); the record rests on evacetrapib, whose transgenic-mouse lipid prediction held in patients while its outcome trial (ACCELERATE) found no benefit.
label: Hyperlipidemia (CETP)

engagement.note: Evacetrapib inhibited plasma CETP ex vivo in human CETP/apoA-I transgenic mice (ED50 under 5 mg/kg) and raised HDL-C. First public 2011, after JTT-705 results in people (2002), so its comparison is a retrodiction.
engagement.quote: In double transgenic mice expressing human CETP and apoAI, evacetrapib exhibited an ex vivo CETP inhibition ED(50) of less than 5 mg/kg at 8 h post oral dose and significantly elevated HDL cholesterol.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed); full text not retrieved.

engagement.note: Healthy volunteers on evacetrapib had 65-91% trough CETP inhibition; retro because the mouse result followed JTT-705 human CETP inhibition (2002).
engagement.quote: The trough inhibition of cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) activity was 65 and 84% at 100 and 300 mg, respectively.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; human study run by the sponsor that made the mouse data.
engagement.reason: CETP activity fell in dosed humans
engagement.judgement: Readout matched to the mouse's own PD readout (ex-vivo plasma CETP activity), so readout_tier direct; the HDL-C rise in patients (Nicholls 2011) is the efficacy endpoint here and is not counted twice. Paired by me: the Suico abstract does not mention the mouse. Mouse ED50 is in mg/kg and human data in mg, with no exposure bridge given, so magnitude direction_only. No NCT record found for this multiple-ascending-dose study (searched LY2484595 and evacetrapib, start before 2011). Retrodiction ruling (2026-11-09): engagement is a claim about the target, and the mouse result (Cao 2011) was first public after JTT-705 cut CETP activity 37% in people (de Grooth 2002, https://doi.org/10.1161/01.CIR.0000015857.31889.7B), so same becomes retro. Teramoto 2014 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amjcard.2014.03.045, April 2014) also shows 50-95% CETP activity falls in Japanese dyslipidaemia patients.

dose.note: Mouse set the effective dose (ex-vivo CETP ED50 under 5 mg/kg); the stated margin came from ZDF rats with no blood-pressure rise at high exposure multiples.
dose.short: Mouse ED50; rat BP margin stated
dose.quote: Importantly, no blood pressure elevation was observed in rats dosed with evacetrapib at high exposure multiples compared with the positive control, torcetrapib.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; exposure multiples not given in the abstract.

dose.note: Humans reached 91% CETP inhibition at 600 mg with no change in 24-h ambulatory blood pressure, so target and margin both held. Margin from the rat BP study run alongside the mouse; Cao 2011 was public before any evacetrapib patient result, so not a retrodiction.
dose.quote: Evacetrapib at the highest dose tested did not produce any significant effect on 24-h ambulatory systolic or diastolic blood pressure.
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the rat study stated a tolerated exposure well above the effective one (no BP rise at high exposure multiples), and humans were dosed to deep CETP inhibition without BP change, so same with margin_stated. The lipid surrogate then responded (efficacy same), so dose is not derived_from efficacy despite the null outcome trial. ACCELERATE's 130 mg later showed SBP +1.2 mmHg vs placebo (NEJM 2017 results text), which the authors call small next to torcetrapib's 5.4 mmHg; I did not count it as a margin failure. Rocacetrapib: an animal allometric PK/PD model (hamster, rat, monkey; Choi 2019, https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics11070336, abstract) predicted a 25 mg efficacious dose but missed human bioavailability badly; it is a different model of a different member and does not change the best-model status, so it is not an entry.
dose.magnitude_basis: CETP inhibition at dose; BP at tolerated exposure

dose.note: Hamster, rat and monkey PK scaled allometrically and linked to an anacetrapib-anchored Emax model predicted a 25 mg daily efficacious human dose.
dose.quote: The predicted PK/PD profile and parameters were used to simulate the human PK/PD profiles for different dose levels, and based on the simulation result, the appropriate efficacious dose was estimated as 25 mg in a 60 kg human.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6680430). Year 2014 is a proxy: the first-in-human study NCT02156544 started 2014-06 at 25 mg, the predicted dose; the model's own date is not stated.
dose.model: Animal allometric PK/PD model (hamster, rat, monkey PK + in-vitro potency), rocacetrapib

dose.magnitude_basis: absolute oral bioavailability (observed under one-fifth of predicted)
dose.note: Observed human bioavailability was under a fifth of the animal-scaled prediction, so predicted exposures and CETP inhibition were not reached at the predicted dose. A retrodiction: published after rocacetrapib phase 1 PK, and it still missed.
dose.quote: The prediction was unsuccessful, as a large discrepancy was highlighted from the observed profiles resulting from misprediction of the absolute bioavailability.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read; the authors give phase 1 data only as figures (FIH unpublished at submission). Human side is the single-ascending-dose study (Kim 2016, https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S120387; NCT02156544, no results posted).
dose.judgement: Dose table row 'target never reached (PK)': at the model's 25 mg the exposure target was missed because absorption was overpredicted, so contra; efficacy for rocacetrapib stays untested (phase 2 NCT02977065 completed 2018 with no results posted). Kim 2020 (https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics12060573), a population model built on human data, recommended 200-400 mg for proof of concept, 8-16x the animal prediction. Not marked retrodiction: the model was built to choose the first-in-human dose and that study began at 25 mg, though its write-up followed the phase 1 data. Main-strip dose status (evacetrapib, same) is untouched; this is a separate track. Retrodiction ruling (2026-11-09): for dose, rocacetrapib's own phase 1 PK (Kim 2016, https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S120387) was public before Choi 2019, so the entry is a retrodiction; it failed to reproduce the human bioavailability, so status stays contra.
dose.model: Animal allometric PK/PD model (hamster, rat, monkey PK + in-vitro potency), rocacetrapib

efficacy.note: Mice carrying human CETP and apoA-I were the in-vivo model for evacetrapib's HDL-raising effect. First public 2011, after JTT-705 results in people (2002), so its comparison is a retrodiction.
efficacy.quote: In double transgenic mice expressing human CETP and apoAI, evacetrapib exhibited an ex vivo CETP inhibition ED(50) of less than 5 mg/kg at 8 h post oral dose and significantly elevated HDL cholesterol.

efficacy.note: Evacetrapib raised HDL-C 54-129% (co-primary, LDL-C also met) in 398 patients; retro, as JTT-705 had raised HDL-C in people before the mouse data. ACCELERATE null.
efficacy.quote: Compared with placebo or statin monotherapy, evacetrapib as monotherapy or in combination with statins increased HDL-C levels and decreased LDL-C levels.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed); JAMA full text not read.
efficacy.reason: Lipid surrogate matched; outcomes trial null
efficacy.judgement: The model predicted a lipid surrogate (HDL-C), and in a hyperlipidaemia context the phase 2 co-primary endpoints (HDL-C, LDL-C % change) are the disease's own endpoints, so the status follows them; ACCELERATE (Lincoff 2017, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1609581; NCT01687998, results posted 2018-05-16; HR 1.01, stopped for futility) sets outcome_tested negative. ACCELERATE enrolled high-risk vascular disease, not a lipid-selected population. I did not use the cholesterol-fed rabbit atherosclerosis model: it was run with non-member drugs (JTT-705, torcetrapib) and I found no evacetrapib atherosclerosis study or statement that Lilly relied on it. Paired by me; the JAMA abstract does not cite the mouse. Mouse HDL rise is not quantified in the abstract, so direction_only. Retrodiction ruling (2026-11-09): efficacy is a claim about the target, and the mouse result was first public (2011) after a CETP inhibitor raised HDL-C in people (JTT-705, de Grooth 2002, https://doi.org/10.1161/01.CIR.0000015857.31889.7B; torcetrapib 2004), so same becomes retro. Design: co-primary endpoints HDL-C and LDL-C, both met; monotherapy arms against placebo plus statin-combination arms against statin alone, scored on the monotherapy comparison, so combination_with is null. DRL-17822 in patient_trials is context only: no DRL-17822 preclinical model is public, so it is not on this track.

patient_trials.quote: Although the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor evacetrapib had favorable effects on established lipid biomarkers, treatment with evacetrapib did not result in a lower rate of cardiovascular events than placebo among patients with high-risk vascular disease.
DRL-17822 phase 2 in type II hyperlipidaemia, primary endpoint percent change in HDL-C at 28 days: placebo 3.2%, 50 mg 84.2%, 150 mg 122.1%, 300 mg 160.6% (registry results table).

efficacy.note: CETP-deficient siblings with markedly raised HDL (Brown 1989) made human CETP loss of function the genetic model for inhibition; opener rebased from Thompson 2008 per check adjudication.
efficacy.quote: Using monoclonal antibodies, we show that CETP is absent in two Japanese siblings who have markedly increased and enlarged HDL.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC, PMID 2586614). Thompson 2008 (https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.299.23.2777) later pooled common CETP variants: moderate CETP inhibition genotypes have higher HDL-C and weakly lower coronary risk.
efficacy.model: Human CETP loss-of-function genotypes (common variants, truncating variants)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HDL-C change (per-allele genotype effect vs drug % change)
efficacy.note: Genotypes predicted higher HDL-C with CETP inhibition; evacetrapib raised HDL-C 54-129% and cut LDL-C in dyslipidaemic patients.
efficacy.quote: Compared with placebo or statin monotherapy, evacetrapib as monotherapy or in combination with statins increased HDL-C levels and decreased LDL-C levels.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both sides; Nomura 2017 (Circ Res) full text read via PMC5523940.
efficacy.reason: Lipid surrogate matched; CHD prediction not borne out
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Nicholls does not cite the genetics. Status follows the lipid surrogate (efficacy rule), so same. The genetic model also predicted lower coronary risk; Nomura 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCRESAHA.117.311145) states that comparison after the fact, asking why evacetrapib and two others failed on CHD outcomes despite truncating-variant carriers having OR 0.70; that miss is carried by outcome_tested negative (ACCELERATE, a high-risk vascular population) and not scored as a status, as for the mouse track. Genotype effect is per allele and far smaller than the drug's, so direction_only. Genetic model dated to Brown 1989 (check adjudication), before any CETP-inhibitor patient result, so the 2011 evacetrapib match is prospective: same, not retro.

patient_trials.quote: Although the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor evacetrapib had favorable effects on established lipid biomarkers, treatment with evacetrapib did not result in a lower rate of cardiovascular events than placebo among patients with high-risk vascular disease.

efficacy.model: Human CETP loss-of-function genotypes (common variants, truncating variants)

safety.model: Rat blood pressure + human adrenal H295R cells
safety.note: Unlike torcetrapib, evacetrapib raised neither rat blood pressure nor aldosterone or cortisol synthesis in adrenal H295R cells: a stated prediction of no off-target harm.
safety.short: Predicted no BP or aldosterone rise
safety.quote: Importantly, no blood pressure elevation was observed in rats dosed with evacetrapib at high exposure multiples compared with the positive control, torcetrapib.

safety.model: Rat blood pressure + human adrenal H295R cells
safety.note: Dyslipidaemia patients on evacetrapib up to 500 mg had no adverse effects (2011); Teramoto 2014 patients and Suico 2014 volunteers showed no BP or mineralocorticoid change.
safety.quote: Although the study was underpowered, no adverse effects were observed.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract states no adverse effects without naming blood pressure. Teramoto 2014 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amjcard.2014.03.045) and Suico 2014 abstracts name BP and mineralocorticoids explicitly.
safety.reason: No torcetrapib-like BP harm in humans
safety.judgement: The model's stated prediction was absence of torcetrapib's off-target BP and aldosterone effect; healthy volunteers bore it out. ACCELERATE (12,092 patients, 130 mg) found SBP 1.2 mmHg higher than placebo, which the authors call small against torcetrapib's 5.4 mmHg and unlikely to affect outcomes; I kept same rather than add a partial entry. DRL-17822 phase 2 (NCT01388816) reports vital-sign changes in 1-2 patients per arm, consistent. Paired by me (Suico does not cite the rat data). Moved to Nicholls 2011 under the ruling that this disease's patients decide and the earliest public date counts (was Suico 2014, healthy volunteers, kept as supporting evidence). Teramoto 2014 quote: "Evacetrapib monotherapy or in combination with atorvastatin was not likely to be associated with any significant change in blood pressure and did not have any adverse effects on mineralocorticoid or glucocorticoid measures."
